antioch: Antioch on the Orontes in Syria around AD 50, a large crowded Roman city with a long colonnaded main street, stone buildings and markets, Mount Silpius rising behind, the Orontes river nearby, people in first-century tunics and mantles.
seleucia: Seleucia Pieria, the stone harbor of Antioch on the Syrian coast around AD 50, wooden Roman merchant ships with square sails moored at stone quays, mountains rising behind the port.
salamis: Salamis on the east coast of Cyprus around AD 50, a Roman harbor city with a stone gymnasium colonnade and a Jewish synagogue building, blue Mediterranean sea, people in first-century clothing.
paphos: Nea Paphos in Cyprus around AD 50, the Roman governor's seat by the sea, a stone harbor, villas with mosaic floors and red-tiled roofs, low coastal hills.
perga: Perga in Pamphylia around AD 50, a Roman city on a plain with a monumental gate flanked by two round towers, a colonnaded street with a water channel, the Taurus mountains behind.
attalia: Attalia, the harbor of Pamphylia on the southern coast of Asia Minor around AD 50, a small walled port with wooden ships under steep cliffs and high mountains.
pantioch: Antioch of Pisidia around AD 50, a Roman colony on a high plateau with a stone temple of Augustus, an aqueduct, and a synagogue, wide fields and snowy mountains in the distance.
iconium: Iconium on the fertile Lycaonian plain around AD 50, a walled town of mud brick and stone with gardens and orchards, flat land stretching to distant mountains.
lystra: Lystra around AD 50, a small Roman colony town on a hill in Lycaonia, simple stone and mud brick houses, a small temple of Zeus at the town gate, herds and farmers nearby.
derbe: Derbe around AD 50, a small town on a mound on the Lycaonian plain, simple stone houses, dry grassland and a lone volcanic mountain in the distance.
galatia: The highlands of Phrygia and Galatia in central Asia Minor in the first century, rolling dry hills, a Roman road paved with stone winding through, a few travellers on foot with a donkey.
troas: Alexandria Troas around AD 50, a Roman harbor city on the Aegean coast with stone walls, baths and a harbor full of ships, the island of Tenedos across the water at sunset.
neapolis: Neapolis, the harbor of Philippi on the Macedonian coast around AD 50, a small walled port on a rocky peninsula, wooden ships, green hills behind.
philippi: Philippi around AD 50, a Roman colony with a stone forum and theatre on the side of a hill, the Via Egnatia stone road passing through, a small river with trees outside the city gate.
thessalonica: Thessalonica around AD 50, a busy capital city of Macedonia on a wide bay, stone buildings climbing the hillside, the Via Egnatia road and a harbor with many ships.
berea: Berea around AD 50, a quiet Macedonian town at the foot of green mountains, stone houses with tiled roofs, a synagogue, olive trees and running streams.
athens: Athens around AD 50 seen from the Areopagus rock, the Acropolis with the Parthenon above, temples and statues of gods everywhere in the city below, philosophers in himations talking.
corinth: Corinth around AD 50, a wealthy Roman city with a large forum, the temple of Apollo with stout Doric columns, shops with arches, and the steep Acrocorinth mountain rising behind.
cenchreae: Cenchreae, the eastern harbor of Corinth around AD 50, stone breakwaters, warehouses and wooden merchant ships in a calm bay of the Saronic Gulf.
ephesus: Ephesus around AD 50, a grand Roman city with a marble street leading down to the harbor, a great stone theatre built into the hillside, crowds and merchants.
caesarea: Caesarea Maritima around AD 50, a Roman port city built by Herod the Great, a huge artificial stone harbor with breakwaters, a white palace on a promontory, a theatre by the sea.
macedonia: The green mountains and plains of Macedonia in the first century, a stone Roman road with milestones passing a small village, travellers walking.
assos: Assos around AD 50, a Greek city on a steep hill overlooking the sea, a temple of Athena on the summit, stone city walls, a small harbor far below.
miletus: Miletus around AD 50, a harbor city with a large stone theatre facing the bay, marble stoas, ships at the quay, a gathering of men on the beach at evening.
rhodes: The harbor of Rhodes around AD 50, stone walls and towers around the port, wooden ships under sail, the island's hills behind.
tyre: Tyre around AD 50, a Phoenician island city joined to the mainland by a sandy causeway, two harbors with ships, a long sandy beach outside the city.
ptolemais: Ptolemais on the coast of Galilee around AD 50, a walled harbor town at the northern end of a wide bay, Mount Carmel across the water.
sidon: Sidon around AD 50, an old Phoenician harbor city with stone houses and a small island harbor, fishing boats and merchant ships, mountains of Lebanon behind.
myra: Myra in Lycia around AD 50, a city with rock-cut tombs carved into the cliff face and a stone theatre, its harbor Andriake nearby with large Alexandrian grain ships.
fairhavens: Fair Havens on the south coast of Crete in the first century, a small open bay with a few huts, steep bare mountains, a large grain ship at anchor under a grey autumn sky.
storm: A large first-century Roman grain ship with a single square sail in a violent winter storm on the open Mediterranean at night, huge waves, the crew struggling with ropes, no land in sight.
malta: The rocky coast of Malta in the first century on a cold rainy morning, a bay with rocks and a sandy beach, a wrecked wooden ship on a sandbar, survivors gathering around a fire.
syracuse: Syracuse in Sicily around AD 50, a large Greek and Roman city on the island of Ortygia, a great harbor with ships, stone temples and city walls.
rhegium: Rhegium at the toe of Italy around AD 50, a small harbor town facing the narrow strait, the mountains of Sicily across the water.
puteoli: Puteoli on the Bay of Naples around AD 50, Italy's great grain port with long stone piers, crowds of ships, warehouses, and Mount Vesuvius in the distance.
rome: Rome around AD 60, a huge crowded city of brick and marble, temples on the Capitoline hill, apartment blocks, narrow streets full of people in togas and tunics.
jerusalem: Jerusalem around AD 57 seen from the Mount of Olives, Herod's temple shining white and gold on its vast platform, the Antonia fortress beside it, city walls and houses.
